searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, seven left unspent, none of them the author's. Three were shared: the Bikavér rules and tiers twice and the district's own history once (restricted to egriborvidek.hu, winesofhungary.hu and bor.hu, read as primary through their summaries). The house's own domain was kept out wherever a second, independent source was wanted (standrea.com twice, galtibor.hu twice, thummerer.hu twice, grofbuttler.hu twice). No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and the rules, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was found in no source of this check and rested on the author's reading alone, it was cut or said with less (the cellar of 2004, the 1993 draft, the Nagy-Eged parcels in Merengő, Áldás, the Gál Tibor Kadarka, Síkhegy's months).
Sources whose title or address names a living person were met among the results and are cited neither in the fragment nor here.

tested: Founding 2002, the name after the founder's wife: The Buyer, Taste Hungary and a visit report agree; kept, the wife and founder unnamed.
The first wine: other accounts give 1999 as the first vintage, 1997 only for an award winning Cabernet Sauvignon; the story's first wine of 1997 changed.
Merengő's barrels: 500 litre Hungarian oak confirmed; months 15 (2019, two merchants), 16 (2022, BOR and Falstaff), 17 (2018, Decanter); changed to a range.
Hangács at Demjén: confirmed by a Hungarian review and merchants; that it was the first single vineyard Bikavér confirmed without a year, so 2007 hedged.

The rules: Kékfrankos at least 30 per cent (Decanter, Best of Hungary); 30 to 65 is the Classicus band in one source only; label changed. 1552 legend and 1851 document: Egri Borvidék and Magyar Bor agree. 2023 separate protected designation: Magyar Bor and the district body agree.

wine.label: was Kékfrankos 30 to 65 per cent, the band one source gives for Classicus alone; now at least 30 per cent, as Decanter and a second guide give it for the blend.

story and the founding question: was the family's first wine a Cabernet Sauvignon of 1997; now wines of the late 1990s before the estate, since other accounts give 1999 as the first vintage and 1997 only for an award winning Cabernet Sauvignon; Egerszalók no longer east of Eger but just outside it.
story and card: Hangács in 2007 as the first single vineyard Bikavér hedged as the house's account (a second source confirms Hangács at Demjén as its first single vineyard Bikavér, with no year).

wine.sites: the Nagy-Eged parcels said to shape Merengő cut, found in no source; others: Áldás cut, its tier and barrels unconfirmed; the Grand Superior trap now says such as Hangács and Nagy-Eged, since Agapé is a third.
open: Merengő's blend in words rests on the house's product page for one vintage; listings for 2019 and 2022 differ (Kadarka in 2022), which the record's moving mix allows.

tested: 1984, the founder's dates and death: Index, Origo, Heol and Infostart notices of December 2021 give 1984, death at 78 in December 2021 (1943 agrees) and Winemaker of the Year 1995; but he leased seven hectares from the council in 1984 rather than bought, so changed.
The cellar: hand cut into volcanic tuff (Egri Borvidék, a tourism listing); the century and the second cellar of 2004 found nowhere, cut.

The Nagy-Eged block: field blend of Cabernet Franc, Kadarka, Kékfrankos, Merlot and Syrah planted 2008, picked and fermented together, eighteen months together: an importer and a Hungarian merchant confirm; a south facing block in the middle of the pure limestone hill.
The hill's height: summit 536 to 537 metres, vines about 500 (Wikipedia, Wines of Hungary); reworded.

story: the cellar cut more than a century before and the second cellar of 2004 cut, found in no independent source; the hand cut tuff cellar kept (Eger wine district body and a tourism listing).

wine.sites: the hill rising to about 500 metres reworded, since its summit is about 536 metres and its highest vines about 500; the block now a south facing one in the middle of the pure limestone hill, as an importer's sheet gives it.
questions: the founding stem now asks when the family took on its first vineyards, not bought them.
open: The planting in the proportions of the finished wine rests on the house's own account; the field blend, the joint picking and fermenting and the eighteen months are confirmed by an importer and a Hungarian merchant, while the house's own category page speaks of a year and a half to two years for Grand Superior.

tested: Ornellaia from 1989, cellar hand to chief winemaker: hungarianwines.eu and Wine Spectator (oenologist 1989 to 1998) agree; kept.
Death on 10 February 2005 in a road accident in South Africa, aged 46, 1958 to 2005: Wine Spectator and wein.plus agree; kept.
Founding: 1992, 1993 or a return in 1992 by account; the empty field and the story's both stand.

Pajados: by Ostoros on rhyolite tuff, Kékfrankos and Kadarka with Syrah, Cabernet Franc, Merlot and Pinot Noir, wild fermented, unfined, unfiltered, 500 litre Hungarian oak, 14 months (2021, 2022) and 18 (2017): merchants and an importer; changed to tie the months to their vintages.
The two sites: Bortársaság calls Síkhegy denser and more concentrated, Pajados straighter and more tannic; the record's lighter, supple Pajados changed.

wine.sites: Pajados now placed by Ostoros on rhyolite tuff (an importer's sheet, with the Hungarian National Museum's site record of the Pajdos hill at Ostoros and the geology of the Ostoros rhyolite tuff); Síkhegy now brown soil over rhyolite tuff.
wine.making and the wine question: about fourteen months now tied to the vintages of 2021 and 2022, since the 2017 listing gives eighteen.
wine.ageing and wine.serve: need not be held long and the Burgundy glass for perfume set aside for a plainer window and a large red wine glass, with half an hour in a decanter for a firmer wine.

open: The son's turn of the house towards single vineyards rests on the house's own account; the founding year stays empty between the end of 1992 and 1993.

tested: 1998 and the first generation winemaker: Magyar Bor, the Eger tourism site and Bound by Wine give 1998; one profile has the first eleven hectares planted on the Öreghegy that year and wine at the quarry from 2003; the question stem changed.

Öreghegy Grand Superior from Verpelét and Bolyki és Bolyki Superior: the Hungarian Wine Summit listing and Decanter confirm both.
Phylloxera in 1886 and the Bikavér of the replanting: Egri Borvidék and Magyar Bor agree.

open: The Hungarian Wine Summit listing calls the Öreghegy Grand Superior the winery's flagship; the plan teaches the classic Egri Bikavér as the first tier of the blend, which the region record supports. The read together agent may weigh a rename to Öreghegy Egri Bikavér Grand Superior; not proposed here, since the author did not propose it and the record would need rewriting whole.
The classic Bikavér's barrel time rests on merchant listings of about eighteen months; the record says well over a year.

tested: 1999, Szarkás in 2000, Nagy-Eged in 2003, the Nagykőporos cellar row: Vinoport, Vinopédia, the Eger wine route and bor.hu agree; kept.

The owners: founded under the historic name by a family, new owners from 2009 (Vinoport, The Drinks Business); the bankruptcy is disputed by the former owner; the change of 2009 added without names or the bankruptcy.

The rules of 1997 and 2002: Magyar Bor gives adoption in 1997 after two years of preparation and official force in 2002 (the district's timeline says the origin law came in 2003); the 1993 draft found nowhere and cut.

The blend: merchant listings for Nagy-Eged Superior and Grand Superior vintages give Merlot and Cabernet led blends with Syrah, Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc and Kadarka; the record's wording for the house's 2018 sheet stands.
The others: Egri Kadarka Superior (Garrafeira Nacional) and Egri Pinot Noir Superior (the house) exist; the Kadarka's Nagy-Eged origin unconfirmed, renamed.

wine.sites, story and card: the hill no longer said to rise to about 500 metres; its highest vines reach about 500, the summit some 536.

open: The house's sheet for 2018 lists no Kékfrankos while Decanter gives at least 30 per cent Kékfrankos for every Bikavér; the record states the house's blend for that vintage and does not say the rule held then.

A trade report of 2011 says the house was rescued from bankruptcy in 2009, which its former owner denied; the record says only that new owners came in 2009. The house's Nagy-Eged wine is a Grand Superior in some vintages (2015); a label with a vineyard name on a Superior is attested for 2018 by another house, so the pick stands.

swaps.proposal: The wine's name alone, Egri Bikavér to Pajados Egri Bikavér Grand Superior; house and key kept
swaps.why: No plain Egri Bikavér of the house was found in the listings read, while Pajados is a current, well documented Grand Superior (vintages 2017 to 2023 at merchants, the Hungarian Wine Summit and the house). The new name holds the plan's words. The read together agent changes plan.json's wine to match wine.name.

tension: The region record (REGIONS: eger) calls Kékfrankos a compulsory backbone of Bikavér; true of the rules now (at least 30 per cent, Decanter), but Gróf Buttler's sheet for its 2018 Nagy-Eged Superior lists none, so the rule may not have bound every earlier vintage. Reported, never edited.

The region record says Egri Csillag since 2010, which agrees with Magyar Bor; it does not say that Bikavér and Csillag gained protected designations of their own in 2023, as the records now teach. Reported, never edited.
The region's producers line for St. Andrea calls its Bikavér the modern standard, a judgement the fragment does not repeat.
